## Design of an Artificial Vision System to Detect and Control the Presence of Black Vultures at Airfields

*Hernando González1, Alhm Vera 2, Diego Valle3 1,2,3 Universidad Autónoma de Bucaramanga `hgonzalez7@unab.edu.co avera488@unab.edu.co dvalle@unab.edu.co`

* Corresponding Author

**Abstract. Flying bird detection is important to avoid bird-aircraft collisions for aviation safety. It is a challenging task due to the wide variations in the appearance of flying birds. In order to make up for the shortcomings of human eye surveillance, image detection of birds has become an increasingly important issue in digital image processing. According to the experimental observations, detecting and localizing the birds in the image is hard because it can tackle the conditions wherein the birds shown are diverse in shapes and sizes and most importantly the complex backgrounds, they are in. Deep learning-based methods are very robust for this kind of task. The following article presents a comparison of two deep learning methods architectures: Single Shot Detector + MobilenetV2 and Single Shot Detector + InceptionV2 for detection of birds in the air. We used the training and testing dataset provided by COCO dataset. The results show that MobilenetV2 + SSD outperforms InceptionV2 + SSD in processing time and accuracy.**

**Keywords: Computer Vision, pretrained model, tracking technique, and Image processing.**

[1], deep convolutional networks  [2], bird detection based on motion-based background subtraction  [3] and in turn pre-trained systems such as Yolo V2, V3 and Mask R-CNN [4], among others.

Due to the exigency in the localization of birds, pre-trained systems have been developing an important role in the detection and classification of objects, however, it is necessary to have a balance between accuracy and processing time, that is why architectures such as MobileNetV2 or Inception present acceptable accuracies in low processing times. These pre-trained models use databases such as 'ImageNet'.  [5], ‘Pascal VOC’ [6], ‘COCO Dataset’ [7], among others that have the bird category. The following paper presents a comparison of two deep learning method architectures: Single Shot Detector + MobilenetV2 and Single Shot Detector + InceptionV2 for airborne bird detection. We use the training and test dataset provided by the COCO dataset.

## **1 Introduction**

The safety of aircraft flying in low altitude airspace is of great importance in many applications, such as air rescue, general aviation and airport operations, however many of these airfields are part of semianthropic ecosystems inhabited by wildlife. This causes the coexistence of wildlife and aircraft within the same space, which generates high probabilities of bird collisions with aircraft (engines, windshields, etc.) causing accidents mainly during takeoff and landing. ## **2 Deployment**

As these deep convolutional networks have appeared, the trend has been to create deeper and more complicated networks to gain accuracy, but these advances in accuracy are not always justifiable and make the models less efficient with respect to size and speed. Bird detection at airfields requires short response times, so we chose to compare two hybrid strategies characterized as the fastest in real-time applications: Single Shot Detector, a combined multi-frame object detector, and MobileNet and Inception, two computationally

inexpensive image classifiers [8]. The stages of development are described below.

## **2.1 Database**

It is necessary to have a quality database, the importance is such that the more robust and complete it is the better our model will learn and the better performance it will have, we worked with the database 'COCODATASET' designed for object detection, segmentation and context recognition, it has 1.5 million objects instantiated in its images and 80 categories and 91 subcategories, for this case we discriminated by the category birds and added images of black vultures for both the training set and the validation set. The data set is divided into three sets, one for training, one for testing and one for validation.

## **2.2      Computer vision algorithms**

We chose to compare two hybrid strategies characterized as the fastest in real-time applications: Single Shot Detector, a multi-frame object detector combined with MobileNetV2 and InceptionV2, two computationally inexpensive image classifiers.

discretizes the output space to determine number of frames in a set of predetermined bounding boxes over different aspect ratios and scales per feature map location. [9]. SSD stands out from other object detectors because of its computational speed without significantly decreasing its accuracy.

In Figure 1 we can observe the Single Shot Detector architecture, this architecture adds several convolution layers at the end which allows it to predict displacements to predetermined frames of different scales with a size of 300x 300, each feature layer can produce a fixed set of predictions, for a feature layer of size m x n with p channels, the basic element to predict the parameters of a potential detection is a small kernel of 3 x 3 x p, this produces a score for a category or a shape displacement with respect to the predetermined frame of coordinates. At each of the m x n locations where the kernel is applied, an output value is produced. [9]. On the other hand, its pyramidal structure in CNN is gradually decreasing layers, this is because SSD does not use a fixed search grid but proposed areas of different proportions that are scaled as it goes through the entire structure of the architecture, this is reflected in its speed above other multi-frame object detectors.

**Single shot detector.** By its acronym SSD,

**Fig. 1.** SSD: Detector Multibox de disparo único [Wei Lio, et al. 2016]

Each feature layer can produce a fixed set of detection predictions, thanks to the set of convolutional filters, i.e. in each of the m x n locations where the kernel is applied, an output value can be obtained (Conv5_3, Conv6, Conv7, Conv8_2, Conv9_2, Conv10_2, Conv 11_2), each convolutional layer is going to get an output in terms of bounding boxes which at the end are summed up as the total number of SSD detections and pass directly to the classifier, during training the actual box is matched with the predicted one to

determine the intersection over union (IoU) value, the boxes exceeding the threshold of 0. 5 will be marked as positive. Another feature that makes it stand out from other locators in speed is the implementation of "no-maximum suppression" to group the overlapping boxes into one and the technique called "hard negative mining" to balance the categories during training, i.e. only uses a subset of negative examples or false positives in each iteration of training maintaining a 3:1 ratio between negative and positive, which allows greater assertiveness in the company of an "extra

feature layers" that are feature maps that help the structure to identify objects of different sizes.

**Mobilenet V2.** Mobilenet is a series of image classifier networks based on TensorFlow and designed to be efficient in mobile devices, this convolutional neural network allows using its architecture and weights to be the basis of new models, for this reason it is part of the pre-trained architectures. Figure 2 describes the architecture of Mobilenet, all the layers are followed by Batchnorm and a Relu activation function, except for the final layer that has a Softmax layer that allows it to perform the classification.

**Fig. 2.** MobileNets Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications [Andrew G. Horward, et al. 2017]

The improvement made in MobileNet version 2 is based on a residual structure, where residual connections help gradients to have better access to the network. The intermediate expansion layer uses light depth convolutions to filter features as a source of nonlinearity. In addition, it was found that it is important to remove nonlinearities in the narrow layers to maintain representational power, this improves performance and provides intuition that led to a better design. [10] Its improvement is represented in the processing speed because the amount of operations (Multiply-accumulate operations MAC) is reduced from 569 million in MobileNetV1 to 300 million in MobileNetV2, and the amount of parameters per million is reduced from 4.24 in MobileNetV1 to 3.47 in MobileNetV2, on the other hand, its accuracy is still higher in MobilenetV1 of 70.9 and in MobileNetV2 is 71.8.

**Inception V2.** Like MobileNet, Inception is also a low computational cost convolutional network with only about 5 million parameters which represented a significant reduction with respect to its predecessor AlexNet which used 60 million parameters. Figure 3 shows the architecture of Inception, which is made up of 9 modules containing 6 layers divided into 3 convolutional layers and an AveragePooling layer, a linear layer and a last softmax layer, it has 22 depth layers, 27 grouping layers, 2 Maxpooling layers that allow finding the maximum value between a sample window and is defined as a summary of area characteristics, reducing processing times, 1 AveragePooling layer which takes the average of the sample window and 1 linear layer. At the beginning of the grid, there are three traditional starting modules in the 35 × 35 with 288 filters each and this is reduced to a grid of 17 × 17 with 768 filters using the grid and so on successively throughout the entire structure.

**Fig. 3.** Inception Recurrent Convolutional Neural Network for Object Recognition

Inception_V2 is made efficient by reducing convolutional sequences of dimension, by means of asymmetric convolutions that are present in the inception modules, the design of each module was made taking into account that convolutional neural networks benefit from the extraction of features at different scales, but essentially what is sought is to reduce computational complexity without losing accuracy, the goal that was raised with the second version of inception, was to reduce the loss of information caused by drastically altering the input dimensions to the network, to achieve this we used intelligent methods of factorization and worked on the efficiency of convolutions in terms of convolutional complexity. [11].

A series of videos were made in order to validate the operation of the architecture from the Jetson Nano. ## **4. Conclusion**

As future work and to apply improvements in the algorithms we could integrate techniques such as the union of convolutional neural networks and support vector machines and in turn apply it to security cameras to prevent the presence of black vultures in areas not allowed, or apply Kalman filters to improve the extraction of the image before passing it through our computer vision algorithms, finally we propose as future work to apply a 3d

preprocessing to the image to generate a more realistic scenario and even to reconstruct the entire environment.
